explanation: The proof builds the inverse power series with PowerSeries.invOfUnit and PowerSeries.mul_invOfUnit, truncates it, and uses PowerSeries.trunc_trunc_mul and PowerSeries.trunc_one. That takes several steps, so it is not a one- or two-line instantiation. I searched Mathlib for a statement that a polynomial with unit constant coefficient has an inverse modulo X^(m+1) (the product minus 1 has zero coefficients up to m). I tried IsUnit with coeff 0 or constantCoeff, divisibility by X^n of a product minus 1, and the uses of invOfUnit. I only found the power-series inverse lemmas and the Nilpotent unit criteria, none of which states this truncated-inverse result.
